# Pinned reference stack for the corpus's fixture author. This is a LOCK file: the full transitive
# closure is pinned so a rerun of `make_fixtures.py` cannot silently pull a newer writer whose
# defaults change a fixture's `s=` attributes — the frozen block lists are hand-derived from exactly
# those bytes. `openpyxl` is the third-party writer that authors every fixture here; FSA1 must never
# be its own oracle input, so nothing in this corpus is generated by FSA1.
#
# Deliberately IDENTICAL below this line to conformance/presentation/requirements.txt,
# conformance/serde/requirements.txt and conformance/xl-oracle/requirements.txt, so all four corpora
# author and grade under one reference stack. openpyxl is the only package this corpus imports; the
# rest of the closure comes with the shared stack and is pinned rather than pruned, because a pruned
# copy is a second reference free to drift. Regenerate with `pip freeze > requirements.txt` only when
# that shared reference is deliberately rev'd, and rev all four in the same change.
#
# This corpus needs no venv: its grader is Rust and runs under `cargo test --workspace`, and the
# fixtures are committed. The pins are what a REGENERATION is held to.
formulas==1.3.4
openpyxl==3.1.5
numpy==2.5.1
numpy-financial==1.0.0
scipy==1.18.0
schedula==1.6.15
click==8.4.2
et_xmlfile==2.0.0
python-dateutil==2.9.0.post0
regex==2026.7.10
six==1.17.0
tqdm==4.69.0
